prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: for each parent category, what is the average selling price per unit, that is the category's total net revenue divided by its total units sold? Round to 2 decimals. Return two columns, in this order: parent_category and revenue_per_unit_eur. Return one row for each parent category. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check what the outer query averages: each product's own price per unit, with every product weighing the same.
Carry the totals through the derived table instead of a ratio, and divide the summed revenue by the summed units once, in the outer query.
starter_sql:
SELECT t.parent_category, ROUND(AVG(t.revenue_per_unit_eur), 2) AS revenue_per_unit_eur
FROM (
  -- one row per product
  SELECT product_id, parent_category, SUM(net_revenue_eur) / SUM(units) AS revenue_per_unit_eur
  FROM sales
  GROUP BY product_id, parent_category
) AS t
GROUP BY t.parent_category
why_this_works: Summing revenue and units before dividing weighs every unit once, so a product that sold many units counts for more than one that sold few.
